evidence.support_text: Cinnamaldehyde produced sensitization reactions in 8/10 guinea pigs in a guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman, 1969) as reported by Maurer and Kimber (1991) (no further details given).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction and challenge: 3% cinnamaldehyde (concentrations used for both; vehicle not reported). Guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman, 1969) as reported by Ishihara et al., 1986.
evidence.support_text: Extreme sensitization effects were observed in a guinea pig maximization test using 3% cinnamaldehyde for both induction and challenge (Ishihara et al., 1986).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal 0.2% trans-cinnamaldehyde in FCA; occluded patch 2.5% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported). Challenge: occluded 24-h patch with 0.75% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported). Species: Dunkin Hartley guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test with induction via 0.2% trans-cinnamaldehyde in FCA intradermal injections followed by a 48-h occluded patch with 2.5% cinnamaldehyde, and challenge with 0.75% cinnamaldehyde occluded 24-h patch, sensitization reactions were observed in 9/10 and 10/10 guinea pigs (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum with and without FCA; occluded patch 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum. Challenge: occluded 24-h patch with 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum. Species: Hartley guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test using 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum for both induction (intradermal and occluded patch) and occluded challenge, sensitization reactions were observed in 16/20 guinea pigs (Prince and Prince, 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Animals sensitized to cinnamaldehyde were challenged with an occluded 24-h patch with 40% cis-cinnamyl alcohol (vehicle not reported). Species: Dunkin Hartley guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In the same study, animals sensitized to cinnamaldehyde were challenged with 40% cis-cinnamyl alcohol; cross-reactions were observed in 2/10 and 3/10 guinea pigs (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Animals sensitized to cinnamaldehyde were challenged with an occluded 24-h patch with 40% trans-cinnamyl alcohol (vehicle not reported). Species: Dunkin Hartley guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In the same study, animals sensitized to cinnamaldehyde were challenged with 40% trans-cinnamyl alcohol; cross-reactions were observed in 4/10 and 5/10 guinea pigs (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Dunkin–Hartley guinea pigs (10/group). Induction: six intradermal injections of 0.25% cis-cinnamyl alcohol in FCA in shoulder area, followed 6–8 days later by a 48-h occluded patch with 100% cis-cinnamyl alcohol. Challenge: 40% cis-cinnamyl alcohol, 24-h occluded patch on flank, reactions read at 24 and 48 h.
evidence.support_text: Cis-cinnamyl alcohol was tested in a guinea pig maximization test using Dunkin–Hartley guinea pigs (10/group) with induction by 0.25% intradermal and 100% topical. Challenge with 40% cis-cinnamyl alcohol produced one sensitization reaction; no cross-reactions with 0.75% cinnamaldehyde were observed (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Dunkin–Hartley guinea pigs (10/group). Induction: six intradermal injections of 0.25% trans-cinnamyl alcohol in FCA in shoulder area, followed 6–8 days later by a 48-h occluded patch with 100% trans-cinnamyl alcohol. Challenge: 40% trans-cinnamyl alcohol, 24-h occluded patch on flank, reactions read at 24 and 48 h.
evidence.support_text: Trans-cinnamyl alcohol was tested in a guinea pig maximization test with induction by 0.25% intradermal and 100% topical trans-cinnamyl alcohol. Challenge with 40% trans-cinnamyl alcohol resulted in two questionable reactions (equivocal); no cross-reactions with 0.75% cinnamic aldehyde were observed (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs (20/group), 250–350 g. Induction: intradermal 5% cinnamyl alcohol in propylene glycol and Freund's Complete Adjuvant in saline; topical 25% cinnamyl alcohol in propylene glycol; 10% sodium lauryl sulfate 24 h before topical. Challenge: 120 mg/ml cinnamyl alcohol in ethanol, 24-h occluded patch, reactions read 72 h.
evidence.support_text: In the same study, a challenge with 120 mg/ml cinnamyl alcohol in ethanol produced nine sensitization reactions in 20 guinea pigs. Additionally, 15 guinea pigs cross-reacted to cinnamic aldehyde at this dose level, whereas no cross-reactions were observed with cinnamic acid (Weibel et al., 1989).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs (20/group), 250–350 g. evidence.support_text: Cinnamyl alcohol was tested in a skin sensitization study using albino female Ssc:AL guinea pigs (20/group) with induction via intradermal 5% and topical 25% cinnamyl alcohol. On day 21, guinea pigs were challenged with 8 mg/ml cinnamyl alcohol in ethanol. One sensitization reaction was observed at this dose level (Weibel et al., 1989).

evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test with induction using 0.2% cinnamic aldehyde intradermally and 2.5% cinnamic aldehyde occluded patch, cross-challenge with 40% cis-cinnamyl alcohol resulted in 2 out of 10 guinea pigs showing cross-reactions (Basketter, 1992).

evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, intradermal injection of 5% cinnamyl alcohol and topical induction with 25% cinnamyl alcohol in petrolatum, followed by a challenge with a sub-irritant concentration of cinnamyl alcohol in petrolatum, produced sensitization effects in Himalayan guinea pigs (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Male guinea pigs (10/group), 350–400 g. Induction: intradermal and topical 5% cinnamyl alcohol; sodium lauryl sulfate (10% petrolatum) 24 h before topical; challenge: 1% cinnamyl alcohol. Reactions read 24 h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: Cinnamyl alcohol was tested in a guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman, 1969) using male guinea pigs (10/group). Induction was via intradermal and topical 5% cinnamyl alcohol, and challenge was with 1% cinnamyl alcohol. No sensitization reactions were observed with cinnamyl alcohol; no cross-reactions with related materials were observed (Senma et al., 1978).
